title: Ticket detail reads fail after malformed runtime application configuration
customer_impact: Ticket creation remains available, but customer ticket-detail reads return HTTP 500 after an invalid runtime value is supplied for the application ticket-event limit.
scope: API liveness/readiness, Nginx, PostgreSQL, Redis, RabbitMQ, persisted ticket data, release identity, and the API image remain healthy/unchanged. The failing path records a structured configuration_error for APP003_TICKET_EVENT_LIMIT=not-a-number.

timeline.event: Customer-path validation observed HTTP 500 on GET /api/tickets/<id> while ticket creation remained available.
L2 acknowledged and confirmed readiness plus PostgreSQL, Redis, and RabbitMQ health remained green.
L2 confirmed release identity and API image ID were unchanged from the healthy baseline.
Container environment inspection found APP003_TICKET_EVENT_LIMIT=not-a-number; API logs recorded configuration_error for the same setting.
The failing X-Request-ID was correlated through Nginx/API logs, Loki, and Tempo, isolating the failure to application runtime configuration.
The setting was corrected to a supported integer and only the API runtime was recreated on the same release image; Nginx configuration was unchanged.
The original ticket read returned HTTP 200 and full release/customer verification passed on the same release image.

evidence: healthy baseline GET /api/tickets/<id> returns HTTP 200 on the APP-003 exercise image
after runtime config injection, GET /api/tickets/<id> returns HTTP 500 while POST /api/tickets still succeeds
PostgreSQL, Redis, RabbitMQ, Nginx, and /health/ready remain healthy
API image ID is identical before fault injection, during failure, and after recovery
container environment contains APP003_TICKET_EVENT_LIMIT=not-a-number during the incident
API log contains configuration_error naming APP003_TICKET_EVENT_LIMIT and the invalid value
same failing request ID appears in Nginx/API logs, Loki, and Tempo
correcting the setting to a supported integer restores the original ticket read and full customer journey without code rollback
resolution: L2 isolated the failure to malformed runtime application configuration rather than code, proxy, database, cache, queue, or release-image regression. The invalid setting was corrected to a supported integer, the API runtime was recreated using the same image, Nginx was reloaded only to refresh Docker service resolution, and the original customer path plus complete release verification passed.
